SMALL AIRPORTS. ELECTRIC POSSIBILITIES. ✈️⚡

The next chapter of electric aviation could have a very familiar home: your local general aviation airport.

An Ohio University study, highlighted by General Aviation News on October 29, examined 37 airports in Ohio, Kentucky and North Carolina. Researchers found that practical electric-aircraft uses could fit existing community needs with relatively modest infrastructure improvements at many locations.

The opportunities include flight training, cargo and emergency services—useful missions that connect aviation to everyday life.

There is work ahead. Thirty of the 37 airports lacked three-phase electrical capacity, a key requirement for high-capacity charging. Airport planning, utility upgrades and workforce training still matter.

This is a study of potential, not an announcement that those airports already offer electric flights. But it points toward an encouraging future: new technology helping small airports serve their communities in more ways. 💛

Sources: Ohio University, October 19, 2026; General Aviation News, October 29, 2026.
